title: Affine-line invariance of finite supported cohomology
statement:
Fix the finite datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$ for arbitrary $n\geq1$. Let $X$ be an arbitrary $k$-scheme (no finiteness or separatedness hypothesis), let $C\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion], put $p:\mathbf A^1_X\to X$ as in [def-sbc-affine-space], and put $C_1=\mathbf A^1_X\times_X C$. With supported cohomology as in [def-pur-support-cohomology], for all integers $q,r$ the canonical projection pullback is an isomorphism
$$p^*:H^q_C(X,A(r))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q_{C_1}(\mathbf A^1_X,A(r)).$$
This holds on the small etale site and on the small pro-etale site for the etale-origin finite twist, compatibly with their canonical comparison. For each section $s:X\to\mathbf A^1_X$ of $p$, the pullback $s^*$ with inverse-image support $C$ is the inverse of this specific map $p^*$. In particular the zero and unit sections induce the same map on these supported cohomology groups. There is no assumption that $X$ or $C$ is smooth, regular, connected, or strictly local.

source.place: Shear paragraph: agent-formulated homotopy lemma replacing the claimed consequence of supported Kunneth. Underlying route is the affine-line acyclicity of sk-prop-a1-kummer, localization (Stacks Tag 09XP), and etale/pro-etale comparison; it does not invoke regular-immersion purity or frame independence. The item applies it to arbitrary etale neighborhoods of an arbitrary smooth $V\to B$ of $k$-schemes, so no finite-type hypothesis is imposed; the unit's acyclicity of the affine line with its base-change compatibility (stalks at geometric points) and localization for $X$ and $X\setminus C$ give the general case.

proof.text: All cohomology groups in this proof have the fixed coefficient twist $A(r)$; its restrictions are understood. Put $U=X\setminus C$ and $U_1=\mathbf A^1_X\setminus C_1=\mathbf A^1_U$. The ordinary affine-line isomorphism of [lem-pur-affine-line-ordinary-invariance] applies to $X$ and $U$ with the restricted twist. Use [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] for $(X,C)$ and $(\mathbf A^1_X,C_1)$. Pullback and compatibility with restriction and boundaries in [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality] give a commutative diagram of these localization sequences. In its five-term segment $H^{q-1}(X)\to H^{q-1}(U)\to H^q_C(X)\to H^q(X)\to H^q(U)$, all vertical arrows except the middle one are isomorphisms by the ordinary lemma. This works on each small site. The comparison clause of [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality] identifies the support pullbacks and connecting maps on the two sites, and the ordinary lemma identifies the ambient and complement pullbacks.

proof.text: Here is the exact-sequence comparison for the diagram in Step 1, writing its two rows as $L\to M\xrightarrow{\delta}S\xrightarrow{j}T\xrightarrow{k}V$ and primed letters, with vertical maps $f_L,f_M,f_S,f_T,f_V$. For injectivity, if $f_S(x)=0$, injectivity of $f_T$ gives $j(x)=0$, so $x=\delta(y)$. Since $\delta'(f_M(y))=0$, write $f_M(y)$ as the image of $l'\in L'$. Lift $l'$ using surjectivity of $f_L$; injectivity of $f_M$ then shows $y$ comes from $L$, hence $x=0$. For surjectivity, take $x'\in S'$. Lift $j'(x')$ to $t\in T$ via $f_T$. Its image in $V$ is zero by injectivity of $f_V$, so $t=j(x)$ for some $x\in S$. Now $x'-f_S(x)$ lies in $\ker j'=\operatorname{im}\delta'$. Lift its preimage in $M'$ using surjectivity of $f_M$ and add its boundary to $x$. This produces a preimage of $x'$. Thus the canonical $p^*=f_S$ is bijective in every degree on both sites, with the comparison compatibility already established in Step 1.

source.place: Shear paragraph: affine-line acyclicity, localization, and comparison of pullbacks along the zero and unit sections.

proof.text: For any section $s:X\to\mathbf A^1_X$ of $p$, the composite $p\circ s$ is the identity of $X$.  By the identity and composition clauses of [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality], the supported pullbacks satisfy $s^*\circ p^*=\operatorname{id}$ (with inverse-image support $s^{-1}(C_1)=(p\circ s)^{-1}(C)=C$).  Since $p^*$ is an isomorphism by Step 2, this $s^*$ is its inverse.  Applying this to the zero and unit sections gives the same inverse map for both sections, as asserted.
